# ThinFilm material database. Wavelengths in micrometres throughout.
# Choosing a material copies it into the design; editing this file never
# changes a design already made from it.
#
# The coefficients are ARCoatingDesigner's (catalogs/Coatings/StandardCoatings.coat).
# The three Sellmeier sets match published fits, and their RANGE is the range of
# the data each fit was made to; please check these against the papers before
# relying on them. The four Cauchy sets record no origin and no range in that
# file, so they are given none here: a RANGE that was guessed would be worse
# than none, because it would be believed.
#
# Nb2O5 is a measured TABLE (lambda um, n, k), copied from the refractiveindex.info
# database (public domain, CC0), file data/main/Nb2O5/nk/Lemarchand.yml: a 500 nm
# magnetron-sputtered film on BK7. Its k is the film's own UV absorption.
#
# No constant-index material ships (the user's rule, 2026-10-02). Air, n = 1,
# is built in and is not listed here.
#
# Ag Al Au Cr Cu CuO CdTe CdSe GaAs Ge InAs InP LiNbO3 MgF2 (o)/(e) MgO Mo Pd
# Pt Si3N4 SiO TiN Y2O3 are measured TABLEs from Palik, Handbook of Optical
# Constants of Solids, as the user supplied them (2026-10-23). Palik joins data
# sets from several authors, so:
#  - where two overlap at one wavelength the first is kept, and where a second
#    set interleaves the first (a zig-zag) its rows are left out;
#  - where n and k are given at different wavelengths (CuO, CdTe, CdSe, GaAs,
#    Ge, InAs, InP, MgO, Si3N4, SiO, Y2O3) each row's missing value is
#    interpolated - n linearly, k in log(k) - and k is 0 across a stretch
#    where Palik gives none (the material is transparent there);
#  - a few rows' wavelengths are corrected where two of Palik's three columns
#    (eV, 1/cm, um) agree and the third does not. Mo's 1815 eV row has the
#    same typo in eV and 1/cm, and takes its um.
# InP stops at 0.975 um, InAs at 34.5 um and Si3N4 at 0.8266 um: beyond, the
# data has a gap (InP), two sets that cannot be told apart (InAs), or ends
# (Si3N4). CdSe, LiNbO3 and MgF2 are uniaxial: (o) is the ordinary index, (e)
# the extraordinary. Y2O3 has two data sets side by side: the first is used,
# and the second fills its gaps (n at 0.625-0.952 um, k in the near UV and at
# 2.9 and 3.9 um). LiNbO3 from 0.40 to 4.0 um gives n(o) and n(e) side by side
# with k 0, in two interleaved sets; the first is used, the second beyond it.
# MgF2 (o) and (e) are Palik's, beside the Sellmeier MgF2 above: below
# 0.0459 um from his first UV set, from there on from the set that runs on
# into the transparent range.

MATERIAL MgF2
  SELLMEIER 0.48755108 0.001882178 0.39875031 0.008951888 2.3120353 566.13559
  RANGE 0.2 7.0
  SOURCE ARCoatingDesigner; matches Dodge 1984, MgF2 ordinary ray
END

MATERIAL SiO2
  SELLMEIER 0.6961663 0.0046791 0.4079426 0.0135121 0.8974794 97.934
  RANGE 0.21 3.71
  SOURCE ARCoatingDesigner; matches Malitson 1965, fused silica
END

MATERIAL Al2O3
  SELLMEIER 1.4313493 0.0052799 0.65054713 0.0142383 5.3414021 325.01783
  RANGE 0.2 5.5
  SOURCE ARCoatingDesigner; matches Malitson and Dodge 1972, sapphire ordinary ray
END

MATERIAL TiO2
  CAUCHY 2.2 0.03 0.003
  SOURCE ARCoatingDesigner; origin and valid range not recorded there
END

MATERIAL Ta2O5
  CAUCHY 1.97 0.022 0.002
  SOURCE ARCoatingDesigner; origin and valid range not recorded there
END

MATERIAL ZrO2
  CAUCHY 1.92 0.022 0.002
  SOURCE ARCoatingDesigner; origin and valid range not recorded there
END

MATERIAL HfO2
  CAUCHY 1.84 0.018 0.002
  SOURCE ARCoatingDesigner; origin and valid range not recorded there
END
